directions.title: Moving things forward
directions.body: When a task needs a start, clarify the goal and one adjustable next step.

directions.title: Engaging through expression
directions.body: When discussion has not begun, explain the idea and invite responses.

directions.title: Steady support
directions.body: When action needs to continue, check a pace and support people can sustain.

directions.title: Standards and checks
directions.body: When a plan needs implementing, check evidence, standards and easily missed details.

science.title: Model origins: four behavioural directions
science.body: The historical foundations of DISC can be traced to Marston’s 1928 theory, followed by the development of different instruments. FermatMind organises situational choices around D, moving things forward; I, engaging through expression; S, steady support; and C, standards and checks. These directions support discussion of behaviour, not four fixed personality categories. FermatMind’s original 24-item questionnaire is not Wiley’s commercial Everything DiSC instrument.

science.title: Scoring: comparing this attempt’s choices
science.body: The 24 questions cover the six pairs among four directions, with each pair appearing four times. Each answer adds one count to the chosen direction. The four counts total 24, and each ranges from 0–12. Every direction tied for the highest count is retained; nearby scores are not merged into a blended type. With a fixed total, choosing one direction passes over another. Counts therefore compare choices within the set, rather than ability or population percentiles.

science.title: Research evidence: check the specific instrument
science.body: Wiley’s research report concerns its Everything DiSC instrument and does not validate FermatMind’s 24 items. In a DISCUS study of 103 undergraduates, Martinussen and colleagues found that the ipsative and normative versions were not equivalent. This cautions against directly converting scores or sharing validation conclusions across instruments, scoring methods or study populations merely because model names are similar.

science.title: Scope: self-observation and communication
science.body: FermatMind has not established internal consistency, test–retest reliability, structural validity, criterion relationships or Chinese reference norms for this questionnaire. Current results are for entertainment and everyday self-exploration; the scenarios and exercises are editorial suggestions for checking experience. Results are not for clinical diagnosis, hiring or promotion decisions, nor do they establish leadership ability, occupational qualifications or relationship compatibility.
